abstract.p: The invention relates to an arrangement (1) for locking cargo (2) to a deck (3) on board a ship (40). Lateral dividing profiles (4, 4<1>), which are capable of being laid out on the deck (3) and secured to it, and which are so arranged as to form loading lanes (5) between pairs of rows, exhibit lock-accommodating openings (6, 7) to accept rotatable and/or movable locking devices (12; 151) from trailer supports and/or cargo cassettes capable of being parked in the cargo lane (5). Present on the trailer supports and/or load cassettes (11) in question is a mechanism (14) which is connected to the aforementioned locking device (12) for the purpose of releasing it or locking it, in conjunction with which a cargo vehicle (13), which can be driven along and between the dividers (4, 4<1>) is so arranged as to actuate the mechanism when the cargo vehicle in question passes the mechanism.

L'invention porte sur un dispositif (1) d'arrimage d'une charge sur le pont (3) d'un navire (40). Des profilés segmentés (4, 4<1>) pouvant se poser sur le pont et s'y fixer de manière à former des voies de chargement (5) comprises entre des paires de rangées, présentent des ouvertures de verrouillage (6,7) destinées à recevoir des dispositifs de verrouillage tournant et/ou mobiles (12, 151) solidaires des châssis de remorques et/ou des berceaux de chargement (11) pouvant être parqués dans les voies de chargement (5). Les châssis de remorques et/ou les berceaux de chargement (11) comportent un mécanisme relié auxdits dispositifs de verrouillage (12) et permettant de les bloquer ou débloquer en association avec les déplacement des véhicules de transport (13) le long et entre les profilés segmentés (4, 4<1>) lorsqu'ils passent devant lesdits mécanismes.

description.p: Device for a loading deck
The present invention relates to an arrangement for locking cargo to a deck on board a ship.

Previously disclosed arrangements for locking a cargo to a deck are, for example, straps, lines and similar tensioning devices, in conjunction with which use is made of existing cargo fittings in the deck of the ship.

Securing of cargo carriers, for example cargo cassettes, is performed only at each end of a positioned row of cargo carriers with the help of counter-pressure components, while cargo trailers have previously been secured to existing cargo openings with the help of straps, for example, in accordance with the above. These previously disclosed devices did not, however, permit so-called automatic activation of the locking devices, and this has had to be performed manually, which has been dangerous and time- consuming for the personnel responsible for securing the cargo. The aforementioned previously disclosed means also did not effectively permit the close packing of freight.
The principal object of the present invention is thus, in the first instance, to solve the aforementioned problems by simple and efficiently functioning means.

The aforementioned object is achieved by means of an arrangement in accordance with the present invention, which is characterized essentially in that lateral dividing profiles, which are capable of being laid out on the deck and secured to it, and which are so arranged as to form loading lanes between pairs of rows, exhibit either lock- accommodating openings to accept rotatable and/or movable locking devices from trailer supports and/or cargo cassettes capable of being parked in the cargo lane or locking devices capable of lateral displacement from lateral dividing profiles, which are so arranged as to interact with trailer supports, cargo vehicles, cargo cassettes and/or some other cargo capable of being parked in the cargo lane, and in that
present on the trailer support and/or load cassette or laterdl dividing profiles m question is a mechanism which is connected to the aforementioned locking device for the purpose of releasing it or locking it, m conjunction with which a cargo vehicle, which can be driven along and between the dividers, is so arranged as to actuate the mechanism when the cargo vehicle m question passes the mechanism.

The invention, which is illustrated m the drawings, is m the form of an arrangement 1 and 101 which is arranged for the detachable locking of a cargo 2 and 102 to a deck 3 on board a ship 40 and comprises long lateral dividing profiles 4, 4 , which are capable of being set up on the deck 3 and of being locked to the deck 3, which profiles are so arranged as to form cargo lanes 5 between pairs of profiles 4, 4" .. arranged m rows.

The aforementioned lateral dividing profiles 4, 41 appropriately exhibit m accordance with a number of illustrative embodiments channel-like lock-accommodating openings 6, 7, which are situated at the lower end 4A of the profiles to either side of a stand part 8 forming the bottom, from which a number of securing devices 9 project m a direction downwards, appropriately m the form of a laterally extending retaining component 10 attached to an upright 11, which can be tightened from the inside of the profile 4 after
the retaining component 10 has been introduced into a matching opening m the deck 3.

In this
, the profile 4 is clamped securely to the deck 3 and forms lane dividers when driving cargo along it on the deck 3.

The lateral lock-accommodating openings 6, 7 are adapted in size to accommodate rotatable and/or movable locking devices 151, 12 from trailer supports 150 and/or cargo cassettes 11 capable of being parked m the cargo lane 5 on the deck. Present on the trailer support 150 and/or the load cassette 11 m question is a mechanism 14, 154 which is connected to the aforementioned locking device for the purpose of releasing I, CI or locking II, CII the trailer support 150 or the cargo cassette 11. A cargo vehicle 13, 113, which can be driven along and between the profiles 4, 41, is so arranged as to actuate the mechanism 14, 154.

In accordance with the invention illustrated m the drawings m Figs. 9-16, the aforementioned trailer support 150, which is formed appropriately by a portal-shaped support component with a connecting pm 153 on its underside and internally within it, which pm is capable of detachable attachment to a cargo tractor vehicle 113 of the kind m question, has a mechanism 154 capable of actuation by the tractor vehicle. The aforementioned mechanism is so arranged, as a result of actuation by the cargo tractor vehicle 113, as to cause the locking devices 151 m the trailer support stand 150 to be moved into a released position CI m which they are disengaged from the profiles 4, 4 . When the cargo tractor vehicle 113 is disconnected from the trailer support, the locking devices 151 m the trailer support 150 are so arranged as to be positively guided into a locked position CII.

Present m conjunction with this is a spring element 161 m the form of a draw spring, which is so arranged, when m the unactuated position by the cargo
tractor vehicle 113, as to cause the locking devices 151 to move to the locked position CII and into engagement with the profiles 4, 4 and their lock- accommodating openings 6, 7 in the profiles 4, 4 . The aforementioned actuating mechanism 154 is formed by an actuating component 155 capable of being pushed m by the cargo tractor venicle 113, for example by means of its turntable 167, and situated on the side of a kmgpm 153, which actuating component m the case illustrated here is formed by a vertically guided upright which, with its bottom part 155A, is attached m an articulated fashion to a pivoting arm 156. Supported on the top part 155B of the upright is a rotating pulley wheel 183, which is so arranged as to extend along a plane extending m the longitudinal median plane 157 of the trailer support 150. The aforementioned actuating component 155 is attached via cables 159, 160 to the locking device 151 m question and a spring 161.

The function of the aforementioned defined arrangement 101 should have been appreciated from the above description, although briefly it functions as follows: A cargo vehicle 113 reverses m under a trailer support 150 of the kind m question, m conjunction with which the mechanise 154 is caused by the cargo tractor vehicle 113 and its turntable 182 to push m the upright 155. The two cables 159, 160, each of which is attached to the axle 164, 165 of its own deflector pulley 162, 163, are tensioned m conjunction with this. The springs 161, one m each trailer support leg 166, 167, normally try to pull on the locking devices 151 so that they adopt their locked position; see Fig. 13. The locking devices can be m the form of pairs of pivotally mounted blocks 151, each of which is rigidly attached to its own vertical axle 168, 169. Each of the aforementioned axles 168, 169 is rigidly attached to its own horizontal arm 170, 171, which, with the help of an
articulated connecting .ink arm 172, provides simultaneous pivoting of the locking αevices 151.

The link arm 172 has a support 173, to which the spring 161 and the cables 159 and 160 on the other leg are attached. Pulling on the cable m the direction 174 causes extension of the spring 161, m conjunction with which the axles 168, 169 rotate m the locking devices 151 m the associated cavity 175, 176 m the trailer support legs 166, 167, after which the trailer support 150 will have been released from engagement with the locking devices 151 m the matching lock-accommodating openings 6, 7 m tne profiles 4, 4 . The cargo trailer l""1 can then be connected to its kmgpm 178 m a turntaole 179 on the top side 150B of the trailer support 150. After the rig has reversed into the ship between the profiles 4, 4 , the cargo tractor vehicle 113 is disconnected from the cargo trailer and the trailer support 150, m conjunction witn which the upright 155 is caused to be displaced downwards wnen the spring 161 relaxes, and the locking devices 151 are caused to pivot out into the locked position. The arrangement 101 thus has a simple and effective function. The rear part of the cargo trailers is attached securely to the deck 3 cy means of straps 180, which are normally kept rolled up m compartments 181 m the profiles 4, 41.

The nature of the embodiment m accordance with the other drawings 1-8 is such that the cargo cassettes 11 exhibit a centrally ^ocated space 15 to accommodate a cargo vehicle 13, which has lifting means enabling a cassette 11 to be hoisted to the desired level for transport or setting down on the deck 3. Projecting actuating devices 16- 16 are provided and are so arranged as to be actuated by the cargo vehicle 13 as it drives into the inner space of the cassette 15 m both directions of travel 17, 18. A rotating component 19, which is rotatably attached to a rotatable
lockmσ device 12, has a number of such radially projecting pivot pins 16-16 , which are connected to the rotating component 19.

The aforementioned cargo vehicle 13 exhibits lateral stops 20, 21 at each end 13A, 13B of the vehicle to either side of it. The aforementioned stops 20,21 project laterally in order to come up against an actuating device 16- 16 as the cassette 11 passes internally 15 therein.

One part of a laterally projecting pm 16-16 attached to the rotating component 19 is guided m such a way as to be capable of actuation m a V-shaped slot 22 in a flat part of the frame 23 of the cassette 11. The locking device 12 is pivotally 25 connected via a universal joint 24 to a rotating component executed as an axle 19 for the purpose of its lateral displacement.

The V-shaped slot 22 is arranged with its meeting point 26 situated between straight elongated openings 27, 28 which meet one another and extend upwards at an angle facing m a direction downwards directly m line with an aforementioned laterally projecting pm 16-16 . The pm 16- 16° is thus capable of actuation by a spring 29 causing it to be positively guided m a downward direction towards the bottom of the aforementioned V-shaped slot 22, i.e. the aforementioned centrally located meeting point 26. The rotating component 19, which is accommodated internally m a U-shaped frame 30, which is open m an upward direction, m one side 31 of which a horizontal opening 32 is present, through which pins 16-16 project laterally, supports a freely moving ring 33 on its external boundary surface 19A. The ring 33 is provided with, for example, four radially projecting pivot pins 16-16 . A compression spring 29 is accommodated by the rotating component 19 acting between the upper part 33A of the ring 33 of the rotating component and a stop 34 located at a higher point for the purpose of producing compression of the aforementioned ring
33 of the rotating component until it is level with the bottom 2b of the V-shaρeα groove. A slotted sleeve 35 is permanently attached tc the under part 33B of the ring 33 of the rotating component, and a rotation-transmitting component 37 accommodated m the slot 36 is permanently connected to the rotating upright 19.

The ring 33 of the rotating component is capable of axial movement along a section of the aforementioned upright 19, but is positively guided m its direction of rotation, _n conjunction with which the locking mechanism 14 is so arrarged, m conjunction with actuation by a vehicle 13, as to be positively guided towards locking position II and locking position I when an aforementioned vehicle 13 passes below the cassette 11, and the pins 16-16 are caused to rotate witn their lateral stops 20, 21 situated at the front and rear, so that the locking device 12 which is connected to the upright 19 also rotates.

This embodiment should have been appreciated from the above description. The embedments in accordance with Figs. 17-23 differ from those described above and the illustrative embodiments of the invention shown m earlier Figures. The embodiment shown Figs. 17-21 comprises locking devices m the form of a number of long, rail-like locking profiles 251 which are actuated, for example by jacks, causing them to be displaced horizontally m a direction 252 across the cargo- accommodating lanes 204 m question and the lateral dividing profiles 205 set out m pairs.

A mechanism can thus be provided on the trailer support 250 anα/or the load cassette 211 m question or on the lateral diviα g profiles 205 m question, which are not shown the drawings. The aforementioned mechanism is connected to the aforementioned locking device m order to release and lock the locking device. A cargo vehicle which is capable of being driven along the profiles 205 and between
them is so arranged as to actuate the mechanism automatically when the cargo vehicle in question passes the mechanism.

The inventien is not restricted to the illustrative embodiments described above and shown in the drawings, but may be varied within the scope of the Patent Claims without departing from the idea of invention.
